items.title: Crypto Weekly: HTX gets caught up in EU sanctions, BitMEX to shut down
items.summary:
STORY: From the EU's sanctions on Russia to BitMEX shutting down...

This is Crypto Weekly.

:: Crypto Weekly

:: HTX caught up in EU's Russia sanctions

The European Union hit Russia with its largest sanctions package in four years.

EU foreign policy head Kaja Kallas said the measures hit more than 100 banks and cryptocurrency operators.

Crypto exchange HTX go caught up in the move.

The firm was included in a list of 18 companies providing crypto services which the EU said helped Russians evade sanctions.

HTX didn't respond to a request for comment.

:: Coinbase settles lawsuit with U.S. SEC

Coinbase settled a Freedom of Information Act lawsuit against the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission.

That's what the crypto exchange's chief legal officer Paul Grewal said in a Wall Street Journal op-ed.

He announced the agency had lost text messages between former Chair Gary Gensler and other officials.

That after a process the SEC said "automatically wiped" certain data.

Grewal wrote the SEC will pay $150,000 and fix its record-retention policies as part of the settlement. 

:: BitMEX announces it will shut down

And crypto exchange BitMEX announced it will shut down operations in September.

It further urged customers to withdraw their assets.

BitMEX didn't give a reason for the closure but said in a statement the decision followed a strategic review of the business and wider crypto industry by its owner.

The closure comes as crypto prices struggle.

Bitcoin has given up most of its gains from last year after a rally fueled by Trump's election to a second term fell away.
